title: Visualization and Quantification of Cold Intolerance Following Peripheral Nerve Injuries of the Upper Extremity
summary:
Background:
Many patients develop pronounced cold intolerance after peripheral nerve injuries of the upper extremity. Symptoms include pain, abnormal sensations, functional impairment, and reduced tolerance to everyday activities. At present, assessment of cold intolerance relies mainly on subjective patient reports, as objective measurement methods are limited.

Research question:
The aim of this study is to improve the assessment of cold intolerance after nerve injuries and to relate subjective symptoms to objective physiological measurements.

Methods:
A standardized questionnaire assessing cold intolerance (modCISS) is applied in its German version and combined with clinical sensory testing and a newly developed, non-invasive thermographic measurement method. Rewarming of both hands after a defined cold stimulus is recorded and compared with the unaffected side.
conditions: Cold intolerance following peripheral nerve injury of the upper extremity

interventions.name: Observational arm: Patients with peripheral nerve injury of the upper extremity who have undergone nerve reconstruction within the past two years.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Peripheral nerve injury of the upper extremity
- Nerve reconstruction within the past 2 years
- First assessment no earlier than 3 months after trauma
- Full capacity to provide informed consent
- Inclusion independent of age and sex
Exclusion criteria:
- Pregnancy or breastfeeding
- Diabetes mellitus
- Peripheral polyneuropathy or other neurological disorders that may interfere with nerve regeneration
- Inability to provide informed consent
